label: Lab 2 • Preparation • 4 minutes • One per author
title: Prepare one peer test
blocks: Give each reviewer the same task and starting state. Ask for a result; let them choose the steps.
Author ____________________   Tool / version ____________________   Group ____   Letter A / B / C / D
Who is this for? What do they need to do, and why?
Write one short task. Include the starting input and what must stay unchanged.
What visible result will you check?
How will you reset? What will you show if the tool cannot run?
Example task: “Try this texture set on the target crate. Leave the protected crate unchanged.”
Ready check: prepared copies • same version • start state ready • reset ready
Choose a mode: hands-on / recording / paper or Figma. A prototype can test understanding; it cannot verify engine behavior.

label: Lab 2 • Peer review • One sheet per reviewer
title: Test a peer tool
blocks: Reviewer: try the task and say what you expect. Author: watch first. Record any help you give.
Mode: hands-on / recording / paper or Figma     Result: independent / helped / blocked / execution untested
What result are you trying to reach?
What did you do, expect and observe? Where did you need help?
Use a lens that fits your observation. You do not need to answer every question.

Know the task — Is the goal and scope clear?
Guide the eye — Do grouping, spacing and contrast show what matters?
Make actions clear — Can you tell what to click and what state it is in?
Keep a shared visual language — Do labels, colors and controls mean the same thing?
Test the whole workflow — Can you check the result and recover?
One observed strength. One issue or question that matters, and why.
If no issue appeared, say so. Mark anything you could not test. Give this sheet to the author.
10-minute round: task 0:00 • try 0:30 • record and share 2:30 • swap 4:00 • finish and reset 8:00

label: Lab 2 • Reflection • Final 5 minutes • One per author
title: Choose one revision
blocks: Compare your reviews. Preserve a strength, choose one change, and plan a test.
Which strength did a reviewer observe?
Which issue or uncertainty matters most? Cite a peer’s observation and its consequence.
What specific change will you make or investigate?
State the input, action and expected result. Include what must stay unchanged.
What changed or strengthened your judgment? What is still untested?
A serious failure can matter even if only one reviewer sees it. Record the reviews you actually received.
